description: Action catalog, analytics event of a press and the screen-shown event: cases shared by every reader of the contract (schema 9.8.0). Five tables. `formCases`: a parameter value against a form of `x-actions.forms`; `problem` is null when the value passes, otherwise one of `x-actions.problems`. The order of checks is part of the rule: missing (no value or the empty string), then too-long, then the form. A row with `repeat` instead of `value` builds the value: `prefix` followed by `char` repeated until the whole string is `length` characters long; in the other tables an object whose only key is `repeat` stands for such a string wherever a string may stand. `schemaCases`: an action as it lies in a document; `valid` says whether the STRUCTURE of schema 9.8.0 accepts it (a reader that draws without validating must not crash on the invalid ones: the field is ignored, the rest of the action works). `documentCases`: what the builder's validator says about a structurally valid action beyond the structure — `issues` is the list of `{ code, at }` (`at` is the path inside the action); rules that need the document or the data dictionary (does the screen exist, is the data path known) are not in this table. `handedCases`: what the HOST gets. `data` is the flat map the node reads data paths from (own keys only; null and a missing key are absence); `handed` is the action as handed over — `type` as written, `params` after `paramBindings` were applied (the key is absent when there are no parameters), `standard` only for a catalog action performed by the host whose parameters passed the form, `invalid` (`param`, `problem`) when they did not. Never both. The `track` field is not part of the handed action. `flowCases`: a document (`screens` maps a screenId to its presentation, `initial` is the initial screen, `entryPoints` maps a public name to a screenId) started by the host with `entry` (null: no name given); `data` as above. `start` is the state right after the first show. Every step is one thing that happens: `press` — a node of the TOP screen with `action` is activated, drawn inside `instances` (Repeater instances, outer first: the entity prefix and the fields of one record; empty — outside any list), and with `cancelled: true` the host cancels the navigation the reader was about to perform; `restart` — the host starts the flow again with another `entry`; `rerender` — the host renders again with new data, another locale or a re-parsed copy of the same document. After each step: `stack` is the screen stack; `track` is the analytics event the host got (null: none) — exactly once per press and BEFORE anything else; `handed` is the action handed to the host (null: the reader performed it itself or it was inert); `shown` is the screen-shown event (null: none). Within one press the order is: track, then either the handed action or the shown event. A reader fires `shown` exactly once per show, never on a server render and never twice for one show (React StrictMode). UPDATE (before release): in `formCases` a host is two or more labels whose last label (the zone) is letters only (two or more) or punycode `xn--…`, so no IPv4 in any notation and no single-word name passes, and a port is 1…65535 without leading zeros. In `handedCases` a binding to a parameter whose catalog entry says `bindable: false` is ignored (the literal acts), and a `params` entry is skipped unless its key has the schema form (non-empty, no whitespace, not `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`, at most 32 characters) and its value is a string of at most 2048 characters. In `flowCases` a step `newVersion` means: the host renders a NEW version of the same document (same documentId and entry); `screens` (required) maps screenId to presentation, `initial` and `entryPoints` (optional) replace the old ones; when the stack holds a screen the new version lacks, the stack is discarded and the flow starts again from the entry of the new version (a show with cause `entry`, depth 1), otherwise nothing happens. A `press` step with `repeat: true` is the auto-repeat of a held activation key: no action, no analytics event, no show; a reader whose test harness has no keyboard may skip such steps.

writeNote: Write actions (schema 9.19.0): «setValue» puts a literal under a data path, «toggleValue» flips the flag under it. The data is x-actions.write. In writeCases «data» is what the data layers hold under each path for the node, «step» is what the press does; «host» is what the host gets through onWrite (null — nothing). A row with «gate» names a path the write gate of the reader refuses (writablePaths, forbidden segments): the reference still computes the step, the reader writes nothing. A value written as {"repeat": …} is a string of that length. 7.0 is written so on purpose.

hapticNote: Schema 9.25.0 — haptic feedback of a press: «haptic» next to «type» and «track» on any action (rules: x-haptic). A request to the host, once per press, before the action; the reader never vibrates by itself. «hapticCases»: the action and whether the press reached the node of an enabled control; «expect» — the word handed to the host, or null. «hapticSchemaCases» — whether the schema accepts the action.
